sources.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 37, Nitsche boundary penalty method (complete 8-page lecture-note chapter)
sources.locator: Complete chapter, PDF pp. 1–8 / printed pp. 183–190: §§37.1–37.3.3, Theorems 37.6–37.8, Lemmas 37.2, 37.3 and 37.5, Remarks 37.1 and 37.4, and Exercises 37.1–37.5.

read_evidence.method: Inspected the complete 8-page PDF text extracted page-by-page from the existing source cache; reread all pages and the complete proofs of the stability, consistency, energy, nonsymmetric L2, and symmetric L2 results.
read_evidence.scope: Complete Chapter 37, including the displayed forms and signs, mesh-dependent norms, inverse-trace threshold, each proof and exercise, the nonsymmetric boundary defect, the symmetric adjoint-consistency cancellation, and the final bibliographic page.

contents.name: §37.1 Nitsche's Dirichlet form and the symmetric adjoint-consistent form
contents.support: The definition records the full H1-conforming trial space, local face-height scale, nonsymmetric and symmetric signs, and their separately modified loads.

contents.name: Remark 37.1, Robin-boundary extension of the method
contents.reason: This pair is restricted to weak imposition of Dirichlet data; Robin and Neumann boundary families require distinct load, stability, and well-posedness hypotheses.

contents.name: Lemma 37.2, aggregate bound for the boundary consistency flux
contents.support: The local inverse trace is summed with the actual maximum boundary-facet incidence; the local proof uses d+1 rather than the source's sharper d count.

contents.name: Lemma 37.3 and Remark 37.4, penalty threshold and well-posedness
contents.support: The item computes a sufficient threshold from the global cross-term constant and proves positivity by the smallest eigenvalue of a 2 by 2 matrix.

contents.name: Lemma 37.5, consistency and boundedness under normal-trace regularity
contents.support: The energy theorem's consistency identity now uses the proved same-page fractional weak Green and conormal-trace supplier; the harvested source's assumptions and signs are retained.

contents.name: Theorem 37.6(i), quasi-optimal energy estimate
contents.support: A direct zero-residual finite-dimensional comparison proof supplies the estimate under the explicit consistency and stability hypotheses.

contents.name: Theorem 37.6(ii), local H1+r approximation rate
contents.reason: The new same-page interpolation theorem proves the zero-trace P1 comparison-norm special case used for the dual L2 argument, but does not prove the source theorem’s full local high-order primal rate. The energy theorem retains its general 0<t<=r broken-norm approximation premise; the broader interpolation result remains deferred to the finite-element interpolation page.

contents.name: Theorem 37.7, nonsymmetric L2 estimate and half-order boundary defect
contents.support: The item keeps the non-canceling pairing with the adjoint normal flux and applies the proved fixed-domain weighted boundary-flux trace, preserving the half-order defect.

contents.name: Theorem 37.8, symmetric L2 estimate with adjoint consistency
contents.support: The item proves the symmetric duality cancellation and uses the same-page zero-boundary P1 interpolation supplier for the full comparison-norm adjoint error, including the normal-derivative trace.

contents.name: Exercise 37.1, equivalence of the boundary-penalty norm with H1
contents.reason: The page estimates errors directly in its mesh-dependent comparison seminorm and does not infer a uniform full-H1 equivalence constant from this optional exercise.

contents.name: Exercise 37.2, quadratic coercivity inequality
contents.support: The item proves the stronger explicit smallest-eigenvalue lower bound for the relevant two-variable quadratic form.

contents.name: Exercise 37.3, local interpolation proof for the energy rate
contents.reason: The local construction now proves the zero-trace P1 dual interpolation branch, including the normal-derivative term, but this exercise asks for the broader higher-order local primal estimate. That branch remains an explicit premise in the energy theorem and is deferred to the finite-element interpolation page.

contents.name: Exercise 37.4, fractional distributional gradient mapping
contents.reason: The assigned energy and L2 arguments use normal traces and the adjoint Green identity, not the negative Sobolev gradient mapping formulated in this separate exercise.

contents.name: Exercise 37.5, extension of duality estimates to the full discrete space
contents.reason: The authored duality route uses the zero-trace subspace and records its exact approximation hypothesis, so the optional full-space extension is not required.

sources.title: Mika Juntunen and Rolf Stenberg, Nitsche's method for general boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 78 (2009), 1353–1374 (complete 23-page published article)
sources.locator: Complete article, PDF pp. 1–23 / printed pp. 1353–1374: §§1–6, Lemma 2.1, Lemma 3.1, Theorems 3.2 and 3.5, Lemma 3.4, a posteriori Theorems 4.2 and 4.4, traditional-method Theorems 5.1–5.3, numerical examples, and references.

read_evidence.method: Fetched the full Aalto-hosted PDF, extracted all pages with PyMuPDF, and inspected the complete 23-page text, including every proof, numerical-example caption, and bibliography page.
read_evidence.scope: Complete published article. The method's epsilon-to-zero Dirichlet convention, signs and reciprocal penalty parameter, consistency, inverse trace, stability, interpolation statement and energy proof were read in full; the a posteriori, traditional-penalty, and numerical sections were also inspected to disposition them accurately.

contents.name: Lemma 2.1, consistency of the parameterized boundary method
contents.support: At the Dirichlet limit, the local theorem records the Green identity explicitly and matches the symmetric load correction term by term.

contents.name: Equation (2.13), symmetric Nitsche Dirichlet limit
contents.support: The present convention uses a large positive gamma0, corresponding to the source's reciprocal small parameter 1/gamma with 0<gamma<1/CI.

contents.name: Lemma 3.1, discrete normal-flux inverse trace bound
contents.support: The consumer proof derives the boundary normal-flux version from the current published polynomial facet inverse-trace estimate.

contents.name: Theorem 3.2 and Assumption 3.3, ellipticity threshold
contents.support: The local penalty convention is reciprocal to the article's small gamma; the positive-definite quadratic form yields the sufficient threshold.

contents.name: Lemma 3.4, Nitsche-norm interpolation estimate
contents.reason: The article states the full-degree V_h estimate for u in H^sigma with 3/2 < sigma <= p+1 and calls it a well-known interpolation result. This batch now proves the zero-trace P1 special case used by the duality arguments, including the weighted normal-derivative term, but it does not prove the broader p-dependent range or arbitrary high-order/local primal branch; that wider interface remains conditional and is deferred to the interpolation page.

contents.name: Theorem 3.5, a priori Nitsche energy rate
contents.reason: The proof in the article depends on its full-degree Lemma 3.4. This batch proves the zero-trace P1 special case needed for the dual L2 theorem, while preserving the general higher-order/local primal approximation branch as an explicit energy-theorem premise; the full source rate remains deferred to the finite-element interpolation page.

contents.name: Theorem 4.2, a posteriori reliability under saturation
contents.reason: The assigned Nitsche pair concerns coercivity, consistency, energy quasi-optimality and L2 duality, not saturation assumptions or residual a posteriori estimators.

contents.name: Theorem 4.4, local efficiency of the a posteriori estimator
contents.reason: Bubble-function efficiency and data oscillation bounds are separate a posteriori theory outside the assigned Nitsche boundary-enforcement scope.

contents.name: Theorems 5.1–5.3, traditional penalty method error and condition-number estimates
contents.reason: The assignment studies Nitsche's consistent weak enforcement, not the distinct Robin-penalty approximation or its conditioning and estimator restrictions.

contents.name: §6, numerical estimator, adaptive-mesh and condition-number comparisons
contents.reason: These reported computations are not used as proof evidence; the assigned examples instead verify finite exact identities and boundary cases.
